candidate_relations.reason: Meperidine-induced skin and soft-tissue injury is the same object as fibrosis and ulceration from three years of subcutaneous meperidine.
Sjogren syndrome is unsupported: ANA is normal and the ulcers sit at documented meperidine injection sites, not in a sicca pattern.
Wedge biopsy shows foreign-body giant cells, but no polarizable material is seen and the cause is meperidine rather than a retained foreign body.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: histologic foreign-body reaction missing drug cause

candidate_relations.reason: Woody dermal fibrosis is present on both forearms and the abdomen but the label omits ulceration and the meperidine etiology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: fibrosis component missing ulcer and meperidine

candidate_relations.reason: Necrotizing fasciitis is an acute infection; cultures are negative and the process is chronic woody induration after years of injections.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: acute necrotizing infection vs chronic injection injury

candidate_relations.reason: Bilateral deltoid, triceps, and biceps contractures are a mechanical complication of repeated injections, not the primary fibro-ulcerative diagnosis.
Lipodermatosclerosis is a venous-stasis sclerosis of the legs, whereas these plaques are at deltoid, forearm, and abdominal injection sites.
Lobular panniculitis with necrotic adipocytes and foamy histiocytes is the biopsy pattern but does not name meperidine-induced fibrosis and ulceration.
Panniculitis is the parent inflammatory category and lacks the meperidine cause plus the ulcerated fibrotic phenotype.
Squamous cell carcinoma can arise in chronic ulcers, but the abdominal biopsy shows panniculitis and fibrosis without malignancy.
Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis requires renal failure and gadolinium exposure, neither of which is described.
Creatine kinase is only 192 U/L (upper limit 174) and the deltoid muscle biopsy is uninvolved, so the CK rise is not the diagnosis.
Inflammatory myopathy conflicts with a normal aldolase, normal AST/ALT, and a deltoid biopsy showing no muscle involvement.
Seven-year mechanical low-back pain explains why meperidine was used but is not the cutaneous fibrosis-ulceration diagnosis.
Contracture from injected substance captures the restricted shoulders and elbows but omits the necrotic forearm ulcer and panniculitic fibrosis.
Pancreatic panniculitis is an enzymatic fat necrosis syndrome; there is no pancreatitis history and transaminases are normal.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: enzymatic pancreatic panniculitis vs toxic injection

candidate_relations.reason: Chronic pain syndrome with multiple psychotropics and fentanyl is the clinical background, not the injection-site dermatopathology.
Chronic muscle injury conflicts with the deltoid biopsy that showed no muscle involvement; injury is dermal and pannicular.
Chronic pancreatitis is not in the history and does not explain culture-negative ulcers at injection sites.
Fibrosis is a histologic component of the woody plaques but omits ulceration and the meperidine cause required by the reference.
